summary: A step's capacity raises its seat's lane while the seat holds the step, and a step whose raised lane does not fit its host waits blocked with why

replay.detail: No claim or projection changes. A waiting step uses the existing blocked state and reason.

rules.detail: Where lanes are on, a ready step that declares a capacity and is assigned to one of this host's laned seats becomes ready only when the raised lane fits the host's room for lanes (the same accounting as a seat start); until then it is blocked with a reason starting `step lane`, tried again each pass. A step whose capacity would lower the lane of a seat declared outside its publication waits with that reason too. While a laned seat holds such a step (assigned and ready, or claimed), its live slice is raised with systemctl --user set-property --runtime, and set back when it no longer does; admission counts the raised lane.

compatibility.detail: Local to each daemon. An older member runs a declared step in its seat's own lane, and an older run owner does not hold it for room.

downtime.detail: Takes effect when the daemon runs this build on a host with lanes on.

recovery.detail: Reverting stops raising lanes for steps; a slice raised at the time keeps its raise until its seat's next launch.
